name: Acyclic USOs Lift Through Convex Reductions
statement: Let $X$ be ample, let $e$ be active, and let $A=\pi_eX$ and $D=X^{\{e\}}$. If $D$ is convex in $A$, every acyclic USO of $A$ lifts to an acyclic USO of $X$ preserving every old-direction edge orientation. Consequently $X$ is corner-peelable exactly when $A$ is, and $X$ peels to $a$ exactly when $A$ peels to $\pi_ea$. Therefore no coordinate reduction of an ample pc-minimal obstruction or rooted factor is convex in its contraction; in particular no such reduction is a cube.
proof: Convexity makes each cube intersection with $D$ a face and places the nonempty complement in one component of $A\setminus D$. Lift old edges from the given orientation and direct each vertical edge toward the component containing the outgoing neighbours at its base, choosing freely when none exist. The outgoing-cube and unique-sink conditions hold on every cube. Any directed cycle with an old edge would project to a directed closed walk in the acyclic base orientation, while vertical edges alone form a matching. Choosing the final vertical direction toward a prescribed lift proves endpoint transfer; contraction proves the reverse implications.
